notice: Read-only browser lab. Curated question narratives; extraction metrics actually calculated from observed records. No live LLM or enterprise systems.

concepts.name: Mined tonnes
concepts.definition: Tonnes of ore physically extracted before processing or quality adjustment.

concepts.name: Saleable tonnes dispatched
concepts.definition: Finished saleable tonnes dispatched to customers after processing and quality checks.

concepts.name: Dispatch plan
concepts.definition: Approved plan for saleable tonnes dispatched during the reporting window.

concepts.name: Mechanical availability
concepts.definition: Time-based mechanical capacity to operate, excluding operational readiness constraints.

concepts.name: Operational readiness
concepts.definition: Operational capability including shift allocation, standby and dispatch requirements.

concepts.name: Crusher downtime
concepts.definition: Scheduled crushing time unavailable because of a crusher fault or trip.

concepts.name: Ore grade
concepts.definition: Measured iron content of feed material, under a stated assay method.

concepts.name: Recognised expense
concepts.definition: Expense recognised in the general ledger for the accounting period.

concepts.name: Purchase commitments
concepts.definition: Approved financial obligations not necessarily recognised as expenses.

concepts.name: Forecast commitments
concepts.definition: Expected commitments used for the forward-looking financial view.

concepts.name: Maintenance backlog
concepts.definition: Open maintenance work not yet performed, assessed against priority and due date.

concepts.name: Spares lead time
concepts.definition: Expected number of calendar days until a critical replacement part is received.

concepts.name: Near miss
concepts.definition: Safety occurrence with potential to cause harm but no reportable injury.

concepts.name: Recordable injury
concepts.definition: Injury meeting the internal safety recording threshold; excludes near misses.

concepts.name: Isolation permit status
concepts.definition: Governed safety authorisation status for an asset at a specific time.

concepts.name: Project milestone
concepts.definition: A dated delivery commitment or decision gate on a capital project.

concepts.name: Customer obligation
concepts.definition: Binding obligation based on an executed customer contract, distinct from sales aspiration.

concepts.name: Asset identity
concepts.definition: Canonical equipment identity across CMMS, finance asset register and shift systems.

questions.title: Why is production below plan?
questions.ask: Why did Pilbara North miss the June dispatch plan?
questions.lead: June dispatch was 42,800 saleable tonnes against a 46,000-tonne plan: a shortfall of 3,200 tonnes (7.0%). Mine control's 48,100 tonnes mined is a different measure, not an opposing dispatch figure.
questions.insight: Crusher C-17 lost 7.5 scheduled hours, mechanical availability averaged 81%, and feed grade was below assumption. These are plausible contributors, not a quantified causal attribution.
questions.decision: Request Operations and Maintenance to quantify each driver and reconcile grade-to-saleable-tonnes losses before selecting a remedy.

questions.title: Is C-17 really available?
questions.ask: Why do Operations and Maintenance disagree on fleet availability?
questions.lead: Maintenance reports 81% mechanical availability while Operations reports 88% fleet readiness. These have different operational boundaries, so the numbers should not be averaged or marked as a numerical contradiction.
questions.insight: C-17 suffered two trips; four high-priority work orders remain overdue, while the vendor quoted a 12-day lead time. The current sources cannot prove the cause of either availability figure.
questions.decision: Assign Maintenance ownership for the mechanical metric, Operations for readiness and Supply Chain for parts timing. Validate the CMMS alias CR17 → C-17.

questions.title: Why don't costs reconcile?
questions.ask: Why does Finance disagree with Procurement about costs?
questions.lead: $12.4m of recognised expense and $13.7m of purchase commitments are different accounting boundaries and need not match.
questions.insight: Two separate June commitment-forecast records disagree ($13.7m versus $14.2m). Because they name the same metric, site and reporting period, this requires reconciliation of the version and approval history.
questions.decision: Ask the Finance steward to identify the approved forecast version and record a governed effective date.

questions.title: Can we trust the safety position?
questions.ask: Were June safety records consistent for Crusher C-17?
questions.lead: Three near misses and zero recordable injuries are different event classes; there is no inherent numerical contradiction.
questions.insight: The permit register says the C-17 isolation permit was closed at 16:00 on 6 June. A same-time handover says it remained open. This is an unresolved safety-critical assertion conflict.
questions.decision: Escalate to the authorised HSE permit owner and verify the original sign-off before any operational reliance.
